title: The closed-support triangle at every coefficient stage
statement:
Fix a prime $\ell$ invertible in the field $k$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$, its valuation ring $\mathcal O_E$ and uniformizer $\varpi_E$, and $A_{E,n}=\mathcal O_E/\varpi_E^n$ for $n\ge1$, as in [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. In the Weil clause use the finite-field datum of [def-weil-finite-field-fiber]. Let $X$ be a separated finite-type $k$-scheme, let $i:Z\hookrightarrow X$ be
a closed immersion and $j:U\hookrightarrow X$ the complementary open
immersion. Let $\Lambda$ be one of the coefficient stages
$A_{E,n},\mathcal O_E,E,\Qlb$, with the categories $D^b_c(-,\Lambda)$ of
[def-weil-derived-complete-integral-detailed],
[def-weil-rationalization-karoubi],
[def-weil-algebraically-closed-coefficients], the pullbacks of
[def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom] and the direct images $i_*$, $Rj_*$
of [def-weil-derived-direct-image].

1. $Rj_*$ carries $D^b_c(U,\Lambda)$ into $D^b_c(X,\Lambda)$.
2. $i_*:D^b_c(Z,\Lambda)\to D^b_c(X,\Lambda)$ has a right adjoint $Ri^!$;
   it is the exceptional inverse image of
   [def-weil-exceptional-inverse-image] (at $\mathcal O_E$ it is
   $R\varprojlim_n\operatorname{Res}_nRi_n^!K_n$, with reductions
   $Ri_n^!K_n$).
3. For $K\in D^b_c(X,\Lambda)$ the closed exceptional counit and the open
   unit extend to a distinguished triangle
   $$
   i_*Ri^!K\longrightarrow K\longrightarrow Rj_*j^*K
   \longrightarrow i_*Ri^!K[1],
   $$
   with $\operatorname{Hom}(i_*Ri^!K[m],Rj_*j^*K)=0$ for all $m$, so the
   third arrow is unique and the triangle is functorial in $K$.
4. $Ri^!Rj_*G=0$ for $G\in D^b_c(U,\Lambda)$, and the unit
   $Q\to Ri^!i_*Q$ is an isomorphism for $Q\in D^b_c(Z,\Lambda)$.

The same holds on the finite-Tor subcategories $D^b_{ctf}(-,\Lambda)$ of
[def-weil-finite-tor-amplitude]. Let $d=\dim U$ when $U\ne\varnothing$ and put $d=0$ when $U=\varnothing$, using the Krull dimension of [def-kun-topological-krull-dimension]. Assume
$c=\operatorname{cd}_{\rm tor}(k)$ ([def-sc-etale-torsion-cd]) is finite
($c=0$ for $k$ algebraically closed).

- (1') $Rj_*$ carries $D^b_{ctf}(U,\Lambda)$ into $D^b_{ctf}(X,\Lambda)$;
   at $\Lambda=A_{E,n}$ Tor amplitude in $[a,b]$ goes to Tor amplitude in
   $[a,b+2d+c]$, and at $\mathcal O_E$ the same holds for the uniform
   interval of the reductions.
- (2') $Ri^!$ carries $D^b_{ctf}(X,\Lambda)$ into $D^b_{ctf}(Z,\Lambda)$,
   with Tor amplitude $[a,b]$ going to $[a,b+2d+c+1]$ (at $A_{E,n}$, and
   uniformly in the reductions at $\mathcal O_E$).
- (3') $i_*$, $i^*$ and $j^*$ preserve $D^b_{ctf}$ and Tor amplitude
   intervals; hence for $K\in D^b_{ctf}(X,\Lambda)$ all three vertices of
   the triangle of (3) lie in $D^b_{ctf}$.
- (4') For $G\in D^b_{ctf}(U,\Lambda)$ and $Q\in D^b_{ctf}(Z,\Lambda)$,
   $Ri^!Rj_*G=0$ and $Q\xrightarrow{\sim}Ri^!i_*Q$ inside $D^b_{ctf}$.

At $E$ and $\Qlb$ these are (1)–(4), since there $D^b_{ctf}=D^b_c$.

If the complementary immersion pair $(i,j)$ is the base change of a closed immersion $i_0:Z_0\hookrightarrow X_0$ and its open complement $j_0:U_0\hookrightarrow X_0$ over $k_0$, and $\Lambda\in\{E,\Qlb\}$, then $Ri^!$
carries Weil structures ([def-weil-weil-sheaf-complex]) for which the
adjunction is equivariant, and for Weil complexes the three arrows of the
triangle and the unit are Weil-equivariant.

proof.text:
Finite-level setting and open direct image. Interfaces phrased with a global finite-field datum but an arbitrary scheme $T$ are used with an auxiliary finite-field datum of characteristic different from $\ell$; they impose no map from $T$ to that auxiliary field. In the Weil clause alone the datum is the actual base-field datum of the statement. The adic-coefficient interfaces are instantiated with $(A,I)=(\mathcal O_E,(\varpi_E))$: the valuation-ring theorem gives a Noetherian DVR, the quotient theorem gives finite quotients, and [lem-weil-pbc-standard-quotients-perfect], with $n\ge1$, gives the augmented resolution $[\mathcal O_E\xrightarrow{\varpi_E^n}\mathcal O_E]	o A_{E,n}[0]$ in degrees $-1,0$. This verifies perfectness of the ordinary $\mathcal O_E$-module $A_{E,n}$ in the adic datum; it does not identify constant and completed coefficient sheaf categories. All schemes in the assertion are Noetherian: finite type over a field implies Noetherianity, so $j$ is quasi-compact (every open of a Noetherian space is quasi-compact), and is separated. Write $G\cong
u_U^*G'$ with $G'$ bounded constructible, using the constructible-origin equivalence. The comparison for qcqs direct images gives $Rj_*G\cong
u_X^*Rj_{\mathrm{et},*}G'$. For each of the finitely many nonzero $\mathcal H^q(G')$, the open-immersion finiteness theorem makes all $R^pj_*\mathcal H^q(G')$ constructible, with only finitely many nonzero. The truncation spectral sequence and the Serre property then show that $Rj_{\mathrm{et},*}G'$ is bounded constructible. Pulling back by the exact $
u_X^*$ proves (1) at $A_{E,n}$.

source.place: Proof, Finite stage: constructibility of Rj_*

proof.text:
Ambient closed adjoint, constructed before the triangle comparison. Work with either the finite constant ring sheaf $B_X=(A_{E,n})_X$ or the completed ring sheaf $B_X=\widehat{\mathcal O}_{E,X}$. The profinite-coefficient inverse-image theorem identifies $i^{-1}B_X=B_Z$ and $j^{-1}B_X=B_U$, with their specified quotient projections. The ringed open-closed theorem applies because $j$ is quasi-compact. It gives exact $i_*,j_!$, $i^{-1}i_*\cong1$, $j^{-1}i_*=0$, and the ordinary open-closed short exact sequence. The immersion-limit-preservation theorem gives exactness of $i^{-1},j^{-1}$ on these module categories. Write them as $i^*,j^*$ here.
For a $B_X$-module sheaf $N$, put $H_N=\ker(N\to j_*j^*N)$ and $i^!_0N=i^*H_N$. The open counit $j^*j_*\to1$ is the identity on the localized site: at an object $V\to U$ both sides have sections $N(V\times_XU)=N(V)$. Exact $j^*$ and the triangle identity imply $j^*H_N=0$. The ordinary open-closed sequence for $H_N$ therefore identifies $H_N\cong i_*i^*H_N$. Every map $i_*P\to N$ has zero composite with $N\to j_*j^*N$, since its adjoint lies in $\operatorname{Hom}(j^*i_*P,j^*N)=0$. Factoring through this kernel and using $i^*\dashv i_*$ and $i^*i_*\cong1$ gives $\operatorname{Hom}(i_*P,N)\cong\operatorname{Hom}(P,i^!_0N)$, naturally and coefficient-linearly. The kernel construction is a functor; these bijections make it the sheaf right adjoint.
Every additive sheaf functor commutes termwise with the finite sums and differentials in mapping cones, and with shifts, so it is exact on homotopy categories. Take the small skeletons in the project's sheaf universe. The module categories admit functorial degreewise-injective K-injective resolutions. Since $i_*$ is exact, its right adjoint $i^!_0$ preserves K-injectives. The termwise homotopy adjunction and the K-injective Hom calculation thus give $i_*\dashv Ri^!_0$ on the ambient unbounded derived categories, with $Ri^!_0K=i^!_0I_K$ and the derived counit induced by the sheaf counit. The same argument derives $j_!\dashv j^*$ and $i^*\dashv i_*$; the ordinary ringed derived adjunction gives $j^*\dashv Rj_*$. Exact functors are computed termwise, so the closed counit remains an isomorphism on all complexes. On the open, a K-injective model and exact restriction give $j^*Rj_*\cong1$ by the section formula above. No supported triangle has been used to obtain these adjoints.

source.place: Unit sk-prop-sf-localization, adjunctions needed for its Hom(-,L) argument; finite and completed coefficient sheaves

proof.text:
The prescribed Hom(-,K) comparison. Applying the ringed ordinary open-closed short exact sequence termwise to any complex $M$ gives a natural distinguished triangle $j_!j^*M\to M\to i_*i^*M\to j_!j^*M[1]$. Apply $\operatorname{Hom}(-,K)$ and all shifts. The adjunctions of Step 2 rewrite its outer terms as
$$\operatorname{Hom}(i_*i^*M,K)\cong\operatorname{Hom}(i^*M,Ri^!_0K)\cong\operatorname{Hom}(M,i_*Ri^!_0K),$$
$$\operatorname{Hom}(j_!j^*M,K)\cong\operatorname{Hom}(j^*M,j^*K)\cong\operatorname{Hom}(M,Rj_*j^*K).$$
The induced two maps are composition with the closed exceptional counit $e:A=i_*Ri^!_0K\to K$ and the open unit $u:K\to B=Rj_*j^*K$: this follows by substituting the unit/counit formulas for the adjunction bijections and cancelling adjacent unit/counit pairs by the triangle identities. In particular $ue=0$. More generally $\operatorname{Hom}(i_*P[m],Rj_*Q)=\operatorname{Hom}(j^*i_*P[m],Q)=0$ for all ambient inputs and shifts.
Complete the actual counit, not the open unit, to a distinguished triangle $A\xrightarrow{e}K\xrightarrow{v}C\to A[1]$. Hom-out exactness gives a map $\beta:C\to B$ with $\beta v=u$; its ambiguity factors through $A[1]$, whose Hom into $B$ is zero, so this map is unique. Here are the missing details establishing that this comparison is invertible. For $W=i_*P$, composition with $e$ gives a bijection $\operatorname{Hom}(W,A[r])\to\operatorname{Hom}(W,K[r])$ by full faithfulness of $i_*$ and $i_*\dashv Ri^!_0$. The long Hom sequence of the counit cone gives $\operatorname{Hom}(W,C[r])=0$, and orthogonality gives $\operatorname{Hom}(W,B[r])=0$. For $W=j_!Q$, $\operatorname{Hom}(W,A[r])=\operatorname{Hom}(Q,j^*A[r])=0$, so $v$ induces a bijection $\operatorname{Hom}(W,K[r])\to\operatorname{Hom}(W,C[r])$. The open adjunction and the invertible open counit show that $u$ induces a bijection $\operatorname{Hom}(W,K[r])\to\operatorname{Hom}(W,B[r])$. Since $\beta v=u$, $\operatorname{Hom}(W,\beta[r])$ is therefore a bijection on both types of outside vertices.
Let $T$ be a cone of $\beta$. The Hom sequences of this triangle now give $\operatorname{Hom}(i_*P,T[r])=\operatorname{Hom}(j_!Q,T[r])=0$ for every $P,Q,r$. Apply $\operatorname{Hom}(-,T[r])$ to the ordinary open-closed triangle of an arbitrary $M$: the adjacent groups with $i_*i^*M$ and $j_!j^*M$ are zero, hence $\operatorname{Hom}(M,T[r])=0$. Taking $M=T,r=0$ makes $1_T=0$, so $T=0$. Hom exactness applied to its triangle makes composition with $\beta$ a bijection on every Hom group; taking the identities of its source and target constructs a two-sided inverse. Thus $\beta$ is invertible. Equivalently this proves the unit's natural bijection $\operatorname{Hom}(M,C[r])\cong\operatorname{Hom}(M,Rj_*j^*K[r])$ for every $M,r$, induced by a specified map rather than inferred from abstract exactness. Replace $C$ by $B$ using $\beta$. This proves the supported triangle with the two prescribed adjunction maps at finite and completed ambient coefficients. Its connecting map is the one transported through this isomorphism.

source.place: Proof of unit sk-prop-sf-localization: apply Hom(-,L) to the ordinary triangle, rewrite outer terms by adjunction, complete the exceptional counit, identify its cone, and use closed-to-open orthogonality

proof.text:
Finite constructible restriction and the determination interface. Step 3 is an ambient argument, so it does not presuppose boundedness of $Ri^!_0K$. For finite coefficients and constructible $K$, its third term is bounded constructible by Step 1 and pullback preservation. The finite bounded constructible subcategory is triangulated; hence $A=i_*Ri^!_0K$ is bounded constructible. The termwise closed counit of Step 2 gives $Ri^!_0K\cong i^*A$, which is bounded constructible by the pullback theorem. The ambient adjunction restricts to these full subcategories. This proves finite-level (2) and the existence in (3). Closed pushforward preservation and full faithfulness are also supplied by the all-stage closed-unit theorem.
The natural-transformation determination theorem can be applied to the counit $i^*i_*\to1$: both functors are exact, and the degreewise counit commutes with the usual signed shifts. It is an isomorphism on sheaves. The truncation triangle of a bounded-cohomology complex has a shift of its highest cohomology sheaf as last vertex; the first vertex has fewer nonzero cohomology sheaves. Starting with zero, two-out-of-three propagates invertibility to every bounded complex. This spells out the unit's determination tool with the shift hypothesis it actually requires; the cone comparison itself has already been proved for every $M$ in Step 3, without assuming that a transformation is determined by its values on generators.

source.place: Finite constructible restriction after the unit Hom comparison; sk-lem-sf-determination

proof.text: Integral operations and conservativity of reduction. Put $R=\mathcal O_E$. The coefficient theorems make $R$ a DVR with finite residue field and each $A_n$ finite; the current perfect-quotient theorem represents the ordinary $R$-module $A_n$ by the augmented finite free resolution $[R\xrightarrow{\varpi_E^n}R]\to A_n[0]$ in degrees $-1,0$, for every $n\ge1$. Thus it verifies precisely the perfect ordinary-module requirement of the Noetherian adic datum; the DVR and finite-quotient statements supply its remaining ring and finiteness hypotheses (the residue characteristic is $\ell$). The passage to completed coefficient sheaves uses the separate constant/completion equivalence below, not this ring-module theorem. First identify the ordinary completed-sheaf direct image of Step 2 with the integral direct image in the statement. For $f=i,j$, direct-image/derived-limit commutation applied to the completeness tower gives $Rf_*K\cong R\varprojlim_n\operatorname{Res}_n Rf_{*,n}K_n$, with the specified projection maps; its finite-reduction projection comparisons are isomorphisms. This is exactly the functor and tower of [def-weil-derived-direct-image], by [prop-weil-pbc-direct-image-limits], with the constant/completed equivalence identifying the coefficient conventions. Thus the ordinary direct image along either $j$ or $i$ preserves the derived-complete constructible category and commutes with every finite reduction by the integral direct-image constructibility theorem. Integral pullback preserves that category and has the stated finite reductions by the integral pullback theorem. This uses the completed coefficient sheaf, not the constant discrete $R$-sheaf. The constant/completed comparison identifies the two notions of derived completeness used in these cited interfaces. If $C$ is an integral constructible object with every $C_n=0$, its defining completeness triangle is $C\to0\to0\to C[1]$, so $C=0$. Since the integral constructible category is triangulated and reduction is derived tensor, it follows by taking the cone that a morphism between its objects is an isomorphism whenever all its reductions are isomorphisms.

source.place: Proof, Integral stage: operations, uniform boundedness and reduction detection

proof.text: Ordinary and completed pullbacks along the immersions agree on derived-complete objects. The immersion-limit-preservation theorem and the coefficient-ring isomorphism make $i^*,j^*$ exact and product-preserving on completed module sheaves. Countable products on these pro-etale module categories are exact, so their derived products are represented termwise. Use the strict-tower derived-limit theorem and its natural Roos model: exact products represent the derived products, so this model is the shifted mapping cone of the termwise map $1-s$. Applying either exact product-preserving inverse image to this model gives the corresponding model of the inverse-image tower, with the same projection maps. This constructs the natural limit comparison; it does not infer a canonical map from a noncanonical choice of cone. For the coefficient comparison put $R=\mathcal O_E$, $I=(\varpi_E)$ and $P_n=R/I^n$, with $n\ge1$. The changed statement [lem-weil-pbc-standard-quotients-perfect] supplies only the ordinary augmented $R$-module resolution $[R\xrightarrow{\varpi_E^n}R]\to P_n[0]$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-completed-constant-sheaf-reduction] on $X_{\mathrm{proet}}$: $R$ is Noetherian by Step 1, and every $P_n$ is finite, so $B_X=\varprojlim_n\underline{P_n}$ is the completed ring sheaf $R_X$ of the adic datum. That separate theorem sheafifies the ordinary resolution and tensors it with $B_X$; flatness over $\underline R$ and the canonical reduction comparison give an augmented finite-free $B_X$-resolution $[B_X\xrightarrow{\varpi_E^n}B_X]\to(P_n)_X[0]$. For $m\ge n$, the map from the $m$-resolution to the $n$-resolution is multiplication by $\varpi_E^{m-n}$ in degree $-1$ and the identity in degree $0$. It is a chain map since $\varpi_E^n\varpi_E^{m-n}=\varpi_E^m$, and its augmentation is the specified quotient map $P_m\to P_n$. The same formulas survive sheafification and scalar extension. This obtains the completed-sheaf resolution and its quotient maps without identifying the two ambient coefficient categories. Exact inverse image carries this resolution, its tensor with any complex, and its quotient transition maps to the corresponding resolution on the source (equivalently use the canonical derived tensor/pullback comparison). Consequently $i^*(K_n)\cong(i^*K)_n$ and $j^*(K_n)\cong(j^*K)_n$. If $K\cong R\varprojlim_n\operatorname{Res}_nK_n$, this proves the same completeness identity for its ordinary inverse image. It is thus canonically the completed pullback, whose defining derived-limit tower is this tower; the canonical comparisons are its projection comparisons, including the quotient cocycle. The finite pullback-preservation theorem gives constructible reductions in the same uniform cohomological interval. Hence these ordinary pullbacks preserve the precise integral category of the statement. The derived adjunctions of Step 2, restricted to it, agree with the completed adjunctions by their unit/counit mate formulas. In particular integral $j^*Rj_*\cong1$ and $j^*i_*=0$, and the orthogonality calculation of Step 3 holds on the integral constructible subcategories.

source.place: Integral stage: identify ordinary immersion inverse images with completed pullbacks before restricting the unit Hom comparison

proof.text:
Integral constructible restriction and finite reductions of the exceptional counit. Apply the counit-cone Hom comparison of Step 3 to an integral constructible $K$. Its middle and open terms are integral constructible by Steps 5-6, and the full integral constructible subcategory is triangulated. Thus $A=i_*Ri^!_0K$ is integral constructible. The closed counit identifies $Ri^!_0K\cong i^*A$, which is integral constructible by Step 6. Restricting the already constructed ambient adjunction gives $i_*\dashv Ri^!$ on the integral category. This uses no integral fibre of the open unit.
Let $T_n=-\otimes^L_R A_n$. The canonical direct-image projection map is adjoint to counit tensor identity, so the transpose of $T_n\eta_f$ under the pullback and direct-image reduction comparisons is $1$: explicitly the calculation reduces to $\varepsilon_f f^*\circ f^*\eta_f=1$. Thus reduction carries the actual integral open unit to the finite open unit. Reducing the supported triangle of Step 3 therefore gives a distinguished triangle with middle $K_n$ and the specified map $K_n\to Rj_{n,*}j_n^*K_n$. Compare the signed rotations with the finite supported triangle, whose first object is $i_{n,*}Ri_n^!K_n$. TR3 with identities on the middle and open objects gives a triangle morphism; two-out-of-three makes its first component invertible. Applying the exact closed pullback and its invertible counit yields $(Ri^!K)_n\cong Ri_n^!K_n$, preserving the arrow into $K_n$. These comparisons are unique: if $a,a':D\to F_n=i_{n,*}Ri_n^!K_n$ are two first-component maps with the same composite into $K_n$, Hom-into exactness for the rotated target triangle factors $a-a'$ through $B_n[-1]$, where $B_n=Rj_{n,*}j_n^*K_n$. For a closed source $D$, Step 3 makes this factor zero. To check quotient transitions $A_{E,m}\twoheadrightarrow A_{E,n}$ with $m\ge n$, regard the $n$-triangle as an $A_{E,m}$-triangle by exact restriction of scalars. The direct-image/restriction comparison [lem-weil-proetale-direct-image-restriction-of-scalars] identifies its open vertex with $Rj_{m,*}\operatorname{Res}_{m,n}(j_n^*K_n)$, so the same orthogonality and Hom-into factorization apply in this single category. The two composites to its closed vertex both compose with the closed arrow to the canonical reduction map into $K_n$, because the projection comparisons and the open units are natural. They are therefore equal. Hence all quotient transitions commute, not merely the individual objects.

source.place: Integral stage: restrict the counit-cone Hom triangle and compare its finite reductions

proof.text:
Identification with the specified exceptional inverse image. At finite level repeat Steps 2-3 on the small etale sites: the existing ambient closed-adjoint theorem supplies the right adjoint, and the ordinary etale open-closed short exact sequence, applied termwise and passed to its derived triangle, supplies the Hom(-,K) comparison with the same two adjunction maps on all complexes. Exact etale inverse image and exact closed direct image extend the closed counit termwise; the open derived counit and closed/open vanishing are those of the open-fully-faithful theorem. Hence every step of the ambient comparison in Step 3 applies, without needing to test an unbounded object using a merely bounded-below input theorem. Its supported object is bounded constructible by open-immersion finiteness, the truncation spectral sequence, the Serre theorem and cohomology exactness, and the exact closed inverse image identifies the adjoint with the closed pullback of that object. The compactification $Z\xrightarrow{1}Z\xrightarrow{i}X$ makes compact-support direct image equal to $i_*$. Thus this is the etale exceptional adjoint used in the definition of $Ri_n^!$.
Exact comparison pullback, its scheme-pullback comparison, and the canonical counit-mate direct-image comparison identify the middle and open maps of its triangle with those in Step 3 on the pro-etale side. TR3 on signed rotations and triangle-morphism two-out-of-three identify the first objects, preserving their maps into $K$. Applying $i^*$ identifies the finite exceptional functors and their counits; their adjunctions and units consequently agree. At integral coefficients Step 7 identifies the reductions of the restricted ambient adjoint with these finite exceptional objects, compatibly with the quotient transitions. Its completeness now gives $Ri^!K\cong R\varprojlim_n\operatorname{Res}_nRi_n^!K_n$, precisely the integral definition in the item. All representing Hom bijections here come from the adjunction constructed in Step 2, not from a supported fibre.

source.place: Finite stage: etale Hom comparison and comparison to the defined functor; Integral stage: completeness and compatible reductions

proof.text: At both the finite and integral stages, $Ri^!$ is an exact functor, linear over the corresponding coefficient ring. At finite level its $A_{E,n}$-linearity can also be seen directly: under the adjunction a map $P\to Ri^!K$ is sent to its closed pushforward followed by the counit; both operations are linear, so the inverse bijection, and the representing action on maps, are linear. Give it the unique shift structure compatible with the adjunction $i_*\dashv Ri^!$, using the adjunction shift theorem. The closed functor $i_*$ is exact: on the ambient categories it is a derived direct image, and the full finite and integral constructible subcategories are triangulated, and its preservation at each stage was proved above. The shift-compatible-right-adjoint theorem now makes $Ri^!$ exact. Thus all the functors, units, counits and triangle maps constructed so far have compatible exact structures; this supplies the exactness required before scalar localization.

source.place: Proof, Rational stage: justifying exactness before transport

proof.text: Uniqueness of the connecting arrow and of maps of supported triangles, at the finite and integral stages. Write a supported triangle as $A\xrightarrow{e}K\xrightarrow{u}B\xrightarrow{\delta}A[1]$, where $A$ is in the closed image and $B$ in the open direct image. Given $f:K\to K'$, the right-adjoint bijection determines a unique $a:A\to A'$ with $e'a=fe$. TR3 supplies a map $b:B\to B'$ completing $(a,f)$ to a triangle morphism. Its first square on $K$ gives $bu=u'f$. The natural map $Rj_*j^*f$ satisfies the same equation. The difference of the two maps factors through $\delta$ by Hom-out exactness and so is zero, since $\operatorname{Hom}(A[1],B')=0$. Therefore $b=Rj_*j^*f$, proving functoriality. For two choices of $\delta$ with fixed $e,u$, TR3 with the two identity maps gives such a $b$; the same vanishing forces $b=1$, and the last square forces the two connecting arrows to coincide. The closed map is also unique when only $f$ is specified: its difference factors through $B'[-1]$ by Hom-into exactness, and $\operatorname{Hom}(A,B'[-1])=0$. This proves exactly the uniqueness promised by the unit and by (3).

source.place: Proof, Vanishing and unit proof: uniqueness and naturality

proof.text: Coefficient-category identification before rationalization. On each of X, Z and U, finite type over the field gives Noetherianity and finite dimension, and ell is invertible. By [lem-weil-pbc-integral-stratified-perfect-characterization], the full completed-coefficient category of [def-weil-derived-complete-integral-detailed] is exactly the category of [def-weil-pbc-bounded-constructible-complete], including the existence of compatible etale-origin witnesses, with the same completed ring sheaf and reduction functors. Their raw rationalizations therefore agree, with the same objects and Hom modules tensored with E. Use this identification also for the finite-stage categories in Step 12. Rational stage. Apply rational transport to the exact $R$-linear functors and to their units and counits. The identities remain identities, and the Hom adjunction bijections tensor with $E$, so $i_{*,E}\dashv Ri_E^!$ and $j_E^*\dashv Rj_{*,E}$. Distinguished integral triangles remain distinguished under raw scalar localization. Hom orthogonality remains zero after tensoring. For a middle map $f$, the rational adjunction determines the closed map $a$, and TR3 gives an open map $b$. Subtracting the natural open map gives a map factoring through the closed vertex shifted by $1$; rational orthogonality makes that factor zero. Applying this to identity middle and closed maps forces two connecting arrows to agree, and the underlying objects still have the specified integral representatives. This proves (1)–(3) at $E$, without an idempotent completion.

source.place: Proof, Rational stage

proof.text: Coefficient-extension coherence and the algebraically closed stage. For $E\subset L$, scalar extension commutes with $i_*,Rj_*,i^*,j^*$ by the scalar-extension theorem. It carries the open unit to the open unit as follows. Write $S$ for coefficient extension and $\pi:S Rf_{*,E}\xrightarrow{\sim}Rf_{*,L}S$. Under the pullback comparison, the transpose of $\pi S\eta_{f,K}$ is $S(\varepsilon_f f^*\circ f^*\eta_f)=1$, since $\pi$ is the canonical projection mate adjoint to $S\varepsilon_f$. Thus $\pi S\eta_f$ is the $L$-unit; its counit equation is $\varepsilon_{f,L}\circ f_L^*\pi=S\varepsilon_{f,E}$ under that same comparison. This uses the canonical derived tensor/pullback identification, not an arbitrarily chosen isomorphism of the two functors. Thus scalar extension of the supported triangle is a triangle with the prescribed middle and open vertices and maps at $L$. Step 10 gives a unique isomorphism of these supported triangles; applying $i^*$ gives $Ri_E^!K\otimes_EL\cong Ri_L^!(K\otimes_EL)$, preserving the counit. Comparing successive extensions with direct extension, both composites preserve this counit and the middle object, so Step 10 makes them equal. For the unit equation set $L=E$ and use the identity scalar comparison; both supported comparisons preserve the counit and hence are identities by Step 10. For the shift equation compare the scalar-extension comparison at $K[1]$ with its shifted comparison at $K$ under the supplied exact shifts. Both have the same middle and open components, so Step 10 makes their closed components agree too. Exact functors and compatible transformations now descend by the common-stage descent theorem; the Verdier-axioms theorem keeps the triangles distinguished. The finite-stage adjunction bijections commute with extension, and hence induce adjunction bijections on the filtered-colimit Hom groups. Orthogonality passes to these same colimits. This proves (1)–(3) at $\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$ for the specified pair category.

source.place: Proof, Algebraically closed stage

proof.text: At each stage take $H=Ri^!Rj_*G$. The adjunction and orthogonality give $\operatorname{Hom}(N,H)=\operatorname{Hom}(i_*N,Rj_*G)=0$ for every $N$; taking $N=H$ makes $1_H=0$, so $H=0$. Full faithfulness of the closed pushforward gives the isomorphism $Q\to Ri^!i_*Q$ by the closed-unit theorem. This proves (4).

source.place: Proof, Consequences

proof.text: Finite Tor preparation. For $A=A_{E,n}$ and $\kappa=A/(\varpi_E)$, the residue criteria detect Tor amplitude by the cohomological interval of $-\otimes_A^L\kappa$ on the etale and pro-etale constructible categories. Every application below is to a bounded constructible object, already established in Steps 1–4 and 8. Derived pullback is monoidal; the coefficient-ring maps identify pullback of $\kappa$ with $\kappa$. Exact inverse image therefore preserves the interval of the residue tensor, so $i^*$ and $j^*$ preserve Tor intervals. They preserve constructibility by the pullback theorem. The comparison-pullback Tor theorem ensures that an etale origin $G'$ of a pro-etale finite-Tor $G$ has the same Tor interval, and conversely. In particular these assertions do not assume that every bounded constructible $A$-complex is perfect.

source.place: Proof, Residue criterion and clause (3′) for pullbacks

proof.text: The closed pushforward preserves the same Tor interval. Let $P$ on $Z$ have interval $[a,b]$, and put $C=i_*P\otimes_A^L\kappa$. Exactness and monoidality of $j^*$ give $j^*C=0$. For each $r$, the sheaf $\mathcal H^r(C)$ is therefore in the closed image by the essential-image theorem, and its closed unit identifies it with $i_*i^*\mathcal H^r(C)$. Exactness of $i^*$, its monoidality and $i^*i_*P\cong P$ give $i^*\mathcal H^r(C)=\mathcal H^r(P\otimes_A^L\kappa)$, which is zero outside $[a,b]$. Hence $\mathcal H^r(C)=0$ there. Apply the pro-etale residue criterion to the bounded constructible $i_*P$ (closed constructible preservation is included in the all-stage closed-unit theorem). This proves finite-level (3′).

source.place: Proof, clause (3′) for i_*

proof.text: Uniform etale direct-image bound. Set $N=2d+c$. When $k$ is algebraically closed, $c=0$, so the etale direct-image vanishing theorem applied to $j$ gives $R^qj_*M=0$ for $q>N$, for every $A$-module sheaf, with a bound independent of $n$. For a general field with $\operatorname{cd}_{\mathrm{tor}}(k)\le c$, the same inference has the following explicit argument: on the basis of affine etale $V\to X$, the scheme $V\times_XU$ is finite type over $k$ and has dimension at most $d$ by etale local-dimension invariance: the local ring at each point has the dimension of the corresponding local ring on $U$, and the stalk-dimension chain theorem identifies these local dimensions with the lengths of generalization chains. Taking their supremum gives the topological dimension bound. The finite-type torsion-cd theorem makes its cohomology vanish in degrees $>2d+c$. The higher-direct-image sheafification formula then makes $R^qj_*M$ zero on $X$. The forgetful derived-direct-image comparison justifies using the underlying torsion abelian sheaf in this formula. When $U$ is empty the direct image is zero and $N=c\ge0$ works directly, with no use of $\dim\varnothing=-\infty$.

source.place: Proof, clause (1′): the 2d+c vanishing bound

proof.text: Open Tor bound. Let $G$ have Tor interval $[a,b]$, and choose its bounded constructible etale origin $G'$; by Step 14, $G'\otimes_A^L\kappa$ has cohomology only in $[a,b]$. The truncation spectral sequence, with Step 16's vanishing bound, puts $Rj_*(G'\otimes_A^L\kappa)$ in $[a,b+N]$. The projection-formula lemma for a finitely presented constant module applies to $f=j$, $K=G'\in D^-$ and $M=\kappa$: $A$ is Noetherian (indeed Artinian), $\kappa=A/(\varpi_E)$ is finitely presented by a single relation, and the required uniform bound is Step 16. It gives $Rj_*G'\otimes_A^L\kappa\cong Rj_*(G'\otimes_A^L\kappa)$. Exact monoidal comparison pullback and the qcqs direct-image comparison give the same residue interval for $Rj_*G$. This object is already bounded constructible by Step 1; the residue criterion now gives Tor interval $[a,b+2d+c]$. This is (1′); the residue field was not treated as a perfect $A$-module.

source.place: Proof, clause (1′) and Projection formula for kappa

proof.text: Closed exceptional Tor bound. Let $K$ have Tor interval $[a,b]$. By Steps 14 and 17, $j^*K$ has interval $[a,b]$ and $B=Rj_*j^*K$ interval $[a,b+N]$. Tensor the finite supported triangle with $\kappa$; exactness of derived tensor leaves it distinguished. The exact cohomology segment $\mathcal H^{r-1}(B\otimes_A^L\kappa)\to\mathcal H^r(i_*Ri^!K\otimes_A^L\kappa)\to\mathcal H^r(K\otimes_A^L\kappa)$ is zero on the two outside terms whenever $r<a$ or $r>b+N+1$. Apply the exact monoidal $i^*$ and $i^*i_*\cong1$ to identify the residue tensor of $Ri^!K$, giving the same vanishing. Since $Ri^!K$ is bounded constructible by Step 4, the residue criterion gives interval $[a,b+2d+c+1]$. This proves finite-level (2′).

source.place: Proof, clause (2′) at the finite stage

proof.text: At the integral stage use the definition by a single uniform Tor interval for all reductions. Steps 5–6 identify reductions of $Rj_*,i_*,i^*,j^*$ with the finite operations; Step 7 identifies reductions of $Ri^!$. Applying Steps 14–18 at every $n$ gives the same intervals $[a,b]$, $[a,b+2d+c]$, $[a,b+2d+c+1]$, independent of $n$. Thus (1′)–(3′) hold integrally. The finite-Tor categories are full triangulated subcategories by their defining finite/integral triangulated-subcategory theorems, so the supported triangles lie in them, and the adjunction bijections and (4) restrict to them. At $E$ and $\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$ the finite-Tor categories equal the constructible categories by definition. This proves (4′) and all the remaining assertions about finite Tor.

source.place: Proof, Other stages

proof.text: Weil equivariance. Use the stated descent of the whole closed/open pair over $k_0$. The Weil-operation theorem supplies Frobenius comparisons for $i_*,i^*,j^*,Rj_*$ and equivariance of the open unit; all their constructible domains have now been proved. Write $F_K=i_*Ri^!K$. For a Weil complex $(K,\theta_K)$, pull the supported triangle back by the Frobenius automorphism and compare it with the supported triangle of $K$. TR3 and Step 10 give the unique map $\theta_F:g_X^*F_K\to F_K$ extending the given $\theta_K$ and its open counterpart. It is invertible by two-out-of-three. The induced $i^*\theta_F$, combined with the pullback composition comparison, gives $\theta_{Ri^!K}:g_Z^*Ri^!K\xrightarrow{\sim}Ri^!K$. The counit is equivariant by construction. Under the adjunction Hom bijections constructed in Step 2 and identified with the specified functor in Step 8 this action on the right adjoint is the mate of the action on $i_*$, so the adjunction bijections commute with Frobenius; in particular the unit, which corresponds to an identity, is equivariant. Finally Step 10 says the connecting arrow is the unique one completing the first two arrows, so its Frobenius conjugate is itself. This proves equivariance of all three arrows and of the exceptional unit.
